KeyConcern: Figures/raw data/method controls should dominate biomedical experimental assessment.
Statistical consistency and data availability should carry high weight.
Formal notices and publication-record status guide C4-C7 boundaries.
C5/C6 require official wording, identity confirmation, and clear responsibility.
Image anomalies are key in life sciences but do not alone prove intent.
Clinical articles require stronger attention to tables, statistics, and design.
Database evidence helps organize patterns but requires source context.
Methods, statistics, and conclusion boundaries should be jointly assessed.
Raw data and repository availability are central to reproducibility.
Responsibility attribution should remain a hard-logic condition, not simple TRS inflation.
